title: Act IV, Scene I

teacherSummary.text: Paris tells the Friar of the wedding. Juliet arrives and fences verbally with him. Alone with the Friar, she threatens suicide; he gives her a potion that will make her seem dead for forty-two hours and promises to send for Romeo.

segments.activity: Model the close reading of the anchor quotation using the written think-aloud below.
segments.script: First, meaning. I read “That is no slander, sir, which is a truth” slowly and put it in my own words: When Paris says she slanders her face by calling it tearful, Juliet replies that what is true is no slander. Next, craft. I notice her careful double meanings, which let her answer without lying or revealing her secret. The strongest word is “slander”: it means a false accusation, which she says cannot apply to truth. Then, effect. What does Juliet's reply to Paris show? My answer: Juliet avoids Paris's questions with wit and hides her marriage to Romeo; her guarded replies show how alone and clever she must now be.
